artworks.title: Columbia Jay
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of two blue birds perched on a branch. The birds are shown in detail, with long tail feathers and crests on the tops of their heads. They are on top of a branch with green and brown leaves. The top bird holds a small nut or seed in one taloned foot and is pressing it with its beak. The background is plain off-white paper.

artworks.title: Mottled Owl
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three owls perched on a pine branch. It features detailed illustrations of three different owls resting on the branches of a pine tree, complete with green needles and pine cones. The owl at the top left is brown with yellow eyes and intricate feather detailing. The one in the center has reddish-brown plumage with yellow eyes. The third owl at the bottom has white and brown feathers, set against the green pine branches. The composition captures the textures of the owls' feathers and the pine needles with delicate precision.

artworks.title: Marsh Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a large nest made of woven grass and twigs, with three marsh wrens perched around it. The birds have brown feathers with white and black markings. The color palette consists of natural earth tones, primarily browns and greens, accented by light touches of white. The nest is centrally positioned, one bird perches on a thin branch extending from the top left, another bird sits directly on the nest to the right, and the third wren hangs below the nest on the left.

artworks.title: Cow Bunting
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting featuring two birds on a patch of grass. Two birds are depicted in detailed naturalistic style, sitting on a small patch of ground overgrown with green moss and grass. The bird on the left has brown and gray plumage, while the bird on the right displays iridescent blue and brown feathers. They appear to be pecking or inspecting the ground. There is an array of small plants and a few clovers scattered around them. The labeling and numbering suggest this is a scientifically illustrated plate, likely used for ornithological documentation. This painting is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Green-blue or White-bellied Swallow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two swallows in flight against a cloudy sky. The image depicts two birds engaged in an aerial maneuver. They are positioned almost in a mirrored fashion towards one another, both with wings and tails spread wide. The background is composed of soft blue hues and fluffy clouds. There is a feather floating nearby.

artworks.title: Raven
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of a raven perched on a branch with leaves and small buds. The raven is depicted in detail, including its glossy black feathers that have a slight bluish sheen. It faces the left, and its beak is slightly open, revealing its tongue. The raven is sitting on a branch, surrounded by green leaves with some mottled brown patches. Among the leaves are clusters of round, brownish buds or nuts. The background behind the bird and branch is plain beige paper.

artworks.title: Blue Jay
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of three blue jays perched on a branch. The birds have bright blue plumage with small areas of white and black, and they are depicted on a gray branch adorned with green leaves and yellow and pink flowers. The topmost bird is using its beak and foot to break open a small white egg, yolk dripping down towards a second bird below that has its wings partially extended and its beak open. The third bird on the left holds a second egg in its mouth. The background behind the birds and branch is off-white paper.

artworks.title: Canada Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds perched on a branch with large leaves and clusters of pink and white flowers. The color palette includes shades of green, pink, white, yellow, and dark gray. One bird is below a group of blossoms while the other bird is near a cluster of blossoms, facing right.

artworks.title: Chipping Sparrow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Chipping Sparrow perched on a tree branch. The bird has a chestnut crown, gray face, and wings with a mix of browns and blues. The branch is adorned with leaves and white flowers. The composition is detailed and delicate, capturing both the bird and foliage realistically, in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Red-breasted Nuthatch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a tree branch. The image shows two red-breasted nuthatches. One nuthatch is upside down on a vertical branch, while the other is upright on a horizontal branch. Both birds are detailed with distinct markings. The branches have textures with lichen and fungi. The painting aims for naturalistic accuracy, following the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Black Vulture
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two black vultures feeding on the carcass of a deer. The painting depicts two vultures with black feathers and grey heads intently focusing on the lifeless deer lying on a patch of grass. The positioning of the birds and the detailed rendering of their plumage gives a realistic and dynamic impression of them engaging in their natural behavior. The contrast between the dark feathers of the vultures and the brown fur of the deer highlights the scene set against a simple background, emphasizing the subjects.

artworks.title: Canada Jay
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two Canada jays are perched on a branch amidst vibrant oak leaves. Each bird displays distinct plumage of gray and white. The color palette includes earthy tones with deep reds, rusty oranges, soft greens, and muted browns, complemented by the grays and whites of the birds. The birds are positioned near the center, with one facing left and the other facing right, both nestled against the green and rust-colored leaves forming a swirling background pattern.

artworks.title: Two-colored Sparrow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds among plants. The image depicts two sparrow-like birds with brown and white plumage, positioned closely together in a naturalistic setting. The birds are placed among a rich variety of plant life that includes green leaves, red berries, and grasses with slender stalks. The background is plain.

artworks.title: Savannah Finch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image depicts two Savannah Finches perched on branches. The birds have mixed plumage of browns and white, blending with the branches and dried grasses. Red and pink flowers, green leaves, and blades of grass are present in the scene. The branches crisscross diagonally, framing the finches and the foliage.

artworks.title: Hooded Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on branches. The artwork features two Hooded Warblers perched on different types of branches. The upper bird has a yellow underbelly, green wings, and a black hood. The lower bird also has vibrant colors. The branches have green leaves, white flowers, and elongated seed pods. The background is minimalist, focusing on the details of the birds and foliage. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Pileated Woodpecker
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of pileated woodpeckers on a grapevine-covered tree trunk. The piece features four woodpeckers perched on the trunk. One woodpecker is shown with a worm in its beak. The trunk displays patches of peeling bark. Surrounding the birds are vine leaves in shades of green and brown, with clusters of deep blue or purple grapes hanging down.

artworks.title: Downy Woodpecker
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of woodpeckers on a flowering branch. The painting depicts two woodpeckers perched on a branch that is adorned with vibrant red and pink flowers. The birds have black and white plumage against leafy green foliage and bright blossoms. Delicate lines and color nuances highlight the woodpeckers' feathers and the branch they are on. The flowers, with soft pink and red hues, add an elegant touch to the scene.

artworks.title: Blue-Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows three birds perched on a branch. The bird at the top has its wings spread wide. The bird on the left is holding an insect in its beak, while the bird on the right seems to be watching. The color scheme is mainly blue with hints of orange, beige, brown, and green in the branch.

artworks.title: White-crowned Sparrow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds on a branch with green leaves and dark blue berries. The color palette includes green, brown, gray, blue, white, and black. The larger bird is perched on the branch with its head turned left, while the smaller bird sits below, facing forward and partially hidden by leaves and berries. The branch extends diagonally across the image.

artworks.title: Wood Pewee
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: A bird perched on a branch with white blossoms and green leaves. The bird has a brown body, a greenish-brown head, and black feathers with white streaks on its wings. The colors in the image include natural earth tones like browns and greens, as well as bright white for the flowers. The branch extends diagonally from the lower right to the upper left of the image, with the bird facing right, situated in the middle of the branch surrounded by the leaves and flowers.

artworks.title: Ferruginous Thrush
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a scene featuring three birds protecting a nest from a black snake. Three birds are shown around a nest with eggs, set in green foliage. One bird is in flight above the nest, another is confronting the snake approaching the nest. The snake is depicted in the branches, creating tension in the composition. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon's detailed bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Mississippi Kite
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting shows two Mississippi Kites perched on a branch. The scene depicts two birds sitting on a partly moss-covered tree branch. The top bird is viewed in profile with its wings folded and an open beak. The bird below also shows its profile, exhibiting a distinctive plumage pattern with soft gray and blue tones, ruffled feathers, and a pale underside. Both birds have red eyes. The tree branch is rugged and textured, with hanging moss adding to the realism. This artwork is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Warbling Flycatcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds perched on a branch alongside large white magnolia flowers and broad green leaves. The color palette includes varying shades of green for the leaves, touches of brown on the branches, and subtle grays and browns on the birds. The birds are positioned on the branch surrounded by clusters of blossoms and leaves.

artworks.title: Yellow-throated Vireo
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: A bird with a yellow head and throat, gray wings, and white underparts clings to a slender brown branch, which also supports a cluster of white and light gray flowers with large green leaves.
